text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government planning to modernise the police force to tackle latest forms of crime, including drugs and fraud. Proposals are to be presented to the cabinet soon, says Prime Minister Alfred Sant.

- Government studying experts' report on San Raffaele Hospital project started by the former Nationalist government and still in its initial stages. Choice is between stopping it, at a cost of several million dollars in work already done, continuing it in its original form or enlarging it so that the hospital could become Malta's sole general hospital, taking over from 60-year-old St Luke's Hospital. The Malta Medical Association favours the last option, saying medical services should not be split. But that could see the cost of the project rise to over $300 million.
- Armed Forces on the look-out for Albanian refugees fleeing unrest in their country. Two ships carrying hundreds of Albanians made it to Malta some four years ago. The refugees were sent back.
- Malta school in Korce, Albania, damaged in riots. All Maltese leave except three friars.
- Strong response in fund-raising for Nationalist Party television station.
